payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Has the mug identified in the source image been moved to the right of the headphones in the edited image?
node.criteria: Pass if comparison of the source and edited images establishes that the source mug has been relocated to the right of the headphones. A separate right-side mug alone is insufficient. Fail if the source mug can be identified and remains left of the headphones or otherwise has not reached the requested position, or if clear visual evidence establishes that a different mug was added instead of moving the source mug. Return unknown if blur, occlusion, or ambiguous correspondence prevents determining the source mug's identity or final position. Execution or transport failures are not visual evidence of failure.
node.binding: Track the source image's blue mug, initially left of the black headphones with its handle facing left, into the edited image using its visible appearance and scene correspondence. Compare that mug's final position with the headphones in the edited image. Inspect the blurred blue region on the left and both white mug-like objects without automatically substituting the rightmost mug for the source mug.

node_traces.evidence: The source mug is a blue mug with its handle facing left. In the edited image, a blurred blue region remains on the left, while two white mug-like objects are visible near the headphones and on the right. The blur and changed appearance prevent confidently establishing whether the source blue mug was moved or whether either white mug corresponds to it, so its final position relative to the headphones cannot be determined.

response.content: {"text":"The binding already identifies the source mug and explicitly warns against substituting either white mug, so do not relax that identity requirement or infer that the rightmost mug is the moved mug. The trace is valid uncertainty, not a transport/schema/dependency failure; its high confidence does not resolve the correspondence. However, the edited image shows a blurred blue mug-shaped region still on the left and two white mug-like objects, one near the headphones and one to their right. The node should make the decision criterion explicitly assess partial progress as well as completion: distinguish evidence that the source mug has been moved or partly relocated from evidence that it reached the required right-of-headphones position, while retaining unknown when identity or position genuinely cannot be established. Avoid treating blur or changed appearance alone as proof of no progress, and avoid counting an unrelated added mug as progress. This should let the aggregate reflect supported partial progress without forcing a label from ambiguous correspondence."}
